clue.text: Rakish fellow cut by a European, though game

indicators.note: the first word is sliced open by the second piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, rakish man
a Lett is a Latvian, a European by nationality

explanation.surface: A dissolute man is wounded by a foreigner, yet stays plucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like an adjective meaning plucky, but it is the noun definition. 'cut by' puts LETT inside ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling contest played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: The effect of Ulster's involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests the letters of the place name are tangled together and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A comment on the consequences of the Northern Irish province taking part in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' is the anagram signal, rearranging ULSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is an outcome or consequence, the same as an effect.

clue.text: Some refuse full-bodied wine, beneficial as it may be

indicators.note: some of the phrase means only a part of its letters is taken, running across two words

explanation.surface: Turning down a robust red might be good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that the answer lies within 'refUSE FULl-bodied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful is helpful or of benefit.

clue.text: Aim to consume small cod as recommended

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
dorse is the name for a young cod

explanation.surface: Planning to eat a little fish, as advised.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSE, a young cod, is an uncommon word. 'to consume' puts DORSE inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsed means approved or vouched for, as when backed by someone's advice.

clue.text: Can point to the spike

parts.note: a tin is a metal can
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A tin might be directed towards a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, S, E, W are standard crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine is a prong of a fork or antler, a sharp point.

clue.text: Tin-ore working in the east

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked over and refashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: Mining tin ore somewhere in the eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of TIN-ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old name for the countries of Asia, lying to the east of Europe.

clue.text: Taking exercise in the stern, comes a cropper!

indicators.note: in means the exercise piece sits inside the stern piece

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone working out at the back of a ship takes a heavy fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes a cropper' is the idiom for falling badly, but here a cropper is one who cuts crops. 'in' puts PE inside REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper cuts grain at harvest, so it is literally one who crops.

clue.text: Mere lads breaking stones

indicators.note: breaking suggests the words are smashed up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Mere boys smashing rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges MERE LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeralds are green gemstones.

clue.text: He's offered a small boat with a certain hesitation

definitions.note: a person who has offered or tendered something, read as 'he has offered' made a noun

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger one
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A man has been offered a dinghy, and hesitates over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's offered' reads as a passive verb, but it defines a person who offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderer is one who submits a bid or offer, as in a contract tender.

clue.text: Laying out money for second hanging

parts.note: pending means hanging, undecided

explanation.surface: Spending cash on an execution that comes later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' hints at an execution, but it means awaiting decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending is paying out cash.

clue.text: Many swear and a quarter get into a hole

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to aver is to declare or swear
N, north, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Lots of people curse and some go underground.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'many' is a crossword convention from the Roman numeral 100.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavern is a large cave, a hollow in the ground.

clue.text: Subsequently a number may be put sideways

parts.note: later means afterwards, subsequently
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a number

explanation.surface: Later on, some figure might be shifted to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral for 50.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to or towards the side.

clue.text: An art gallery needs a particular means of ventilation

definitions.meaning: a slatted vent or shutter letting air through

explanation.surface: A gallery needs a certain kind of air vent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre is the Paris museum, and a louvre is an arrangement of angled slats for airflow.

clue.text: Inexperienced driver — one given reprimand for causing damage

parts.note: L is the learner plate of a British driver under instruction
an ace is a one in cards
to rate is to scold or reprimand

explanation.surface: A learner driver is told off for crashing the car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L-plate. RATE meaning 'scold' is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or wound flesh, a form of injury.

clue.text: Stipulations made by one section of the orchestra

definitions.meaning: conditions attached to a deal, as in 'no ... attached'
the violins, violas, cellos and basses

explanation.surface: Conditions laid down by one part of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings are conditions attached to an offer, and also the bowed instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: Hide the real outcome

indicators.note: the outcome of the words is a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Conceal what truly happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb but is the noun, animal skin. 'outcome' rearranges THE REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin.

clue.text: The limit, for example, of French backing

indicators.note: backing means the two short words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: An example of French support reaching its limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses EG + DE, giving EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a border or boundary, the point where something stops.

clue.text: A woman advocates choice climbing plants, systematically classified

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
the Bar is the body of barristers, advocates

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-class, choice; read as AI

explanation.surface: A woman lawyer picks out climbing plants and sorts them neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI for letters. 'climbing' reverses AI to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbaria are collections of dried plant specimens arranged and catalogued.

clue.text: Study only when fit again

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
just means only

explanation.surface: Only hit the books once you have recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like 'healthy', but it is the verb, to adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to set or alter something once more.

clue.text: Think to change date and time

indicators.note: to change means the two words' letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Consider rescheduling the appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges DATE and TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or ponder deeply.

clue.text: Key agreement for viewers

parts.note: E is a musical key
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A deal is struck for the television audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a musical key, here E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs of sight.

clue.text: The sailor's back clothed in black and white will be copied

indicators.note: clothed in means the reversed piece is wrapped inside the colour word

parts.note: pied means patched black and white, like a magpie

indicators.note: back means the sailor word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor dressed in monochrome will be imitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TAR to RAT, and 'clothed in' puts RAT inside PIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirated means reproduced illegally, as with films or software.

clue.text: A girl on the river gets extra room

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A young woman by the water acquires more space.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so ANN sits over EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension or additional building attached to a larger one.

clue.text: None inside ran out, though adversely affected

indicators.note: inside means the zero sits within the other piece

parts.note: spilt means poured or ran out, as liquid does
O, a zero, means none

explanation.surface: No one at the crease was run out, though the team suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a batsman 'run out' misleads; 'ran out' is liquid escaping. 'inside' puts O into SPILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilt means damaged or ruined.

clue.text: The crossword compiler's dog?

definitions.meaning: the person who writes a puzzle
a breed of gundog, such as an Irish one

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the puzzle writer owns a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter compiles crosswords, and a setter is also a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Jocularity tolerable only to the adolescent?

definitions.text: Jocularity tolerable only to the adolescent?

parts.words: Jocularity tolerable only to the adolescent?
parts.note: read as three words, the answer describes something poor at a certain stage of life

explanation.surface: Teasing humour that only teenagers can put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as BAD IN AGE: jokes that are bad at any age but the young one.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, witty banter.

clue.text: It's easy for those with faith in natural healing

definitions.text: for those with faith in natural healing
definitions.meaning: a medicinal herb used by herbalists

explanation.surface: Herbal remedies are straightforward for believers.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple means easy, and a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant.

clue.text: Scholars beginning singing in a low voice

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates

indicators.note: beginning means just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Students start to sing deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' picks the S of 'singing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass is the lowest male singing range.

clue.text: Stimulated, or possibly exhausted

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the two pieces may be arranged another way

parts.note: used up means exhausted

explanation.surface: Excited, or perhaps worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link offering a choice, but it is fodder: 'possibly' rearranges OR with USED.
explanation.definitionFit: Roused means stirred up or excited.

clue.text: An individual can't change a lot, so one maintains

definitions.text: An individual can't change a lot, so one maintains

parts.words: An individual can't change a lot, so one maintains
parts.note: describes a person who believes what happens is predetermined and cannot be altered

explanation.surface: A remark that a person cannot alter much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' suggests an amount, but it also means one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes events are fixed by fate and cannot be changed.

clue.text: Man getting excited about the music

indicators.note: about means the jumbled word goes around the next one
getting excited means the word is stirred up and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A man gets worked up about the tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting excited' rearranges MAN to ANM, and 'about' puts it round THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song, such as a national hymn.

clue.text: The chump, to break in on such an agreeable guy!

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a chump
to enter is to go in, break in on

explanation.surface: Barging in on such an obliging fellow is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agreeable' here means one who agrees, not one who is pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: An assenter is someone who consents or agrees.
